cases.visibleGeometry: A broad smooth slope occupies the centre, crossed by diffuse shallow linear traces. Broken gullies fringe the left and right edges. A sharply bounded, roughly quadrilateral raised patch with a flatter top lies in the southeast; several small irregular knobs lie near the west and south edges.
cases.alternatives: The angular patch could be a modern building platform, spoil or water infrastructure. Gullies and linear traces may be erosion, tracks or terrain processing effects.
cases.supportLimits: Most of the patch is measured, with scattered interpolated cells. The angular patch has measured support, but shape and age cannot be established from the model alone.

candidates.feature: Angular raised patch with relatively flat top
candidates.nextCheck: Compare with current and historical imagery, mapped structures, and original ground returns to identify construction or processing effects.

cases.visibleGeometry: Several narrow branching incisions converge near the lower centre, forming a rough Y-shaped drainage pattern. Broad smooth flanks and a few irregular small bumps lie beside the channels. A short straight segment at the west edge meets one incision, but no coherent enclosure or platform is apparent.
cases.alternatives: The incisions fit runoff erosion or drainage modification. The straight segment may be a field boundary, track or model artefact; the small bumps may be rock, vegetation remnants or spoil.
cases.supportLimits: The main channel junction contains a band of interpolated cells, limiting confidence in its detailed shape. Broad surrounding ground is mostly measured.

cases.visibleGeometry: Dense, evenly spaced curved ridges wrap a broad rise on the west; shallower parallel ridges cover the east. A sharp north-south break divides them, meeting an east-west line near the lower third. A compact rounded rise interrupts the eastern ridges near the upper centre-right.
cases.alternatives: Repeated ridges suggest agricultural cultivation or terracing. The straight breaks could be a track, boundary or drainage. The compact rise could be exposed rock, field clearance, soil accumulation or a natural knoll.
cases.supportLimits: The broad surfaces are mostly measured; intermittent interpolation follows the central break and lower line. The compact rise is in largely measured terrain, but the imagery alone cannot resolve its origin.

candidates.feature: Compact rounded rise amid parallel ridges
candidates.nextCheck: Inspect original ground returns and aerial imagery for rock, agricultural clearance or recent disturbance.

cases.visibleGeometry: A largely smooth surface contains several isolated small rises and shallow depressions. One compact irregular cluster lies just east of the patch centre; a more prominent small rise lies in the northwest. Very faint straight traces run between some of the bumps, without a clear enclosure or platform.
cases.alternatives: The bumps may be stones, clearance heaps, vegetation remnants, small natural knolls or modern disturbance. The faint traces may be tracks, cultivation lines or processing artefacts.
cases.supportLimits: The central cluster and most surrounding ground have measured model support, with only sparse isolated interpolation. Their small size still makes interpretation uncertain without raw returns and independent imagery.

candidates.feature: Small irregular cluster of rises east of centre
candidates.nextCheck: Compare original ground returns, aerial imagery and mapped surface features to distinguish stones or clearance from terrain-processing effects.
